note: Anti-NGF antibodies reached IC/BPS on chemical-cystitis rodent models; one small tanezumab POC was positive, the two larger trials (tanezumab dose-ranging, ASP6294) failed, and the class-wide joint-safety hold stopped the program.
label: IC/BPS (anti-NGF)

engagement.model: Chemical cystitis in rats with NGF sequestration (trkA-IgG)
engagement.note: Intravesical NGF reproduced cystitis hyper-reflexia and trkA-IgG sequestration blocked it; IC patient bladders carry raised NGF (Lowe 1997), but no IC trial measured NGF engagement.
engagement.short: Rat bladder NGF, no patient PD
engagement.quote: Administration of exogenous nerve growth factor into the lumen of the urinary bladders of normal anaesthetized rats produced a rapid and marked bladder hyper-reflexia similar to that seen with experimental inflammation.
engagement.reason: No NGF engagement readout in IC trials
engagement.judgement: Patient-side premise exists (Lowe 1997, doi:10.1046/j.1464-410x.1997.00097.x: NGF raised in IC bladder biopsies) but neither tanezumab IC trial nor the ASP6294 trial (PD listed in title; no NGF endpoint in the EU CTR results) reported target engagement, so the cell stays untested.

dose.model: Chemical cystitis in rats with NGF sequestration (trkA-IgG)
dose.note: trkA-IgG 1 mg/kg set no human exposure target; no published model-to-patient exposure bridge for tanezumab's IC doses (200 µg/kg IV; 1–20 mg SC).
dose.short: No model exposure target for IC
dose.quote: Treatment of animals with the fusion molecule at 1 mg/kg, immediately before inflammation of the bladder, largely, and very significantly, prevented the expected increases in reflex excitability of this organ.
dose.judgement: Later rodent work (Hu 2005 REN1820 in CYP cystitis, doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000155170.15023.e5; Guerios 2005/2008 anti-NGF antiserum) also reports fixed doses only; the tanezumab IC doses match its other Phase 2 programs but no source states a model-derived target.

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Irritant cystitis in rats: trkA-IgG prevented bladder hyper-reflexia; later CYP cystitis showed REN1820 and anti-NGF antiserum reverse overactivity and referred hyperalgesia.
efficacy.short: NGF sequestration blocks rat cystitis hyper-reflexia
efficacy.quote: Systemic treatment with the nerve growth factor-sequestering molecule, but not control molecules, partially and significantly reversed established inflammatory changes, by about 30-60%, depending on outcome measure.
efficacy.judgement: Model family chosen as the one the IC programs cite: Dmitrieva 1997 (trkA-IgG, Genentech), Hu 2005 (REN1820, CYP cystitis, doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000155170.15023.e5), Guerios 2005 (CYP, mice, doi:10.1016/j.neulet.2005.09.026) and Guerios 2008 (acrolein, rats, doi:10.1152/ajpregu.00728.2007). None dosed tanezumab, fulranumab or ASP6294; ASP6294's only published pharmacology (Koya 2023, doi:10.1080/19420862.2022.2149055) uses arthritis models.

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Single-dose tanezumab 200 µg/kg cut average daily IC pain by 1.4 points more than placebo at week 6 (n=64), as the cystitis models predicted.
efficacy.short: Tanezumab POC cut IC pain 1.4 points
efficacy.quote: At week 6 tanezumab produced a significant reduction from baseline in average daily pain score vs placebo (treatment difference [LS mean, 90% CI] was -1.4 [-2.2, -0.5]).
efficacy.judgement: Abstract only (paywalled); registry results for NCT00601484 (A4091010, posted 2021-05-13) corroborate: LS mean difference -1.36, 90% CI -2.203 to -0.510. Evans did not put the rodent data beside the trial as far as the abstract shows, so comparison_stated is false; 'same' rests on direction only.

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: ASP6294 320 mg SC (n=119) and tanezumab 1–20 mg SC (n=205, futility) both missed on bladder pain; the model held only in the small POC.
efficacy.quote: Change from Baseline in Average Mean Daily Pain (MDP) Score at Week 12: ASP6294 -2.34 (0.28), placebo -2.13 (0.26); Mixed-Effect Model Repeated Measures (MMRM), difference -0.2, 90% CI -0.84 to 0.43, p = 0.591.
efficacy.judgement: Quote is assembled from registry result fields, not prose. Called contra over same because the class's only adequately sized IC trials both missed: ASP6294 6294-CL-0101 (NCT03282318; CT.gov carries no results, EU CTR posted 2020-02-08) and tanezumab A4091035 (NCT00999518, results posted 2021-08-03: week-8 differences vs placebo -0.03 to -0.23, all 95% CIs crossing zero; terminated 2010-11-16 after the hold and an interim analysis, 'terminated for futility' per Pfizer's 2012 AAC briefing). Year set by the earliest valid source (EU CTR 2020); Nickel 2016 (doi:10.1016/j.juro.2015.10.178) pools A4091010/A4091035 and reports a female-subgroup benefit but its abstract gives no per-trial result. Fulranumab's IC trial NCT01060254 (n=31) was terminated for the hold with no results posted.

safety.model: Rat, mouse and cynomolgus toxicology with joint histology
safety.note: IC POC saw headache and paresthesia, no joint signal; the toxicology package, silent on joints, had not been compared with any patient outcome.
safety.short: Tox silent on joints; POC saw paresthesia
safety.quote: The most common adverse events were headache (tanezumab 20.6%, placebo 16.7%) and paresthesia (tanezumab 17.6%, placebo 3.3%).
safety.judgement: Abstract only. Year of first use of the toxicology models is not given in any source found (they predate the 2008 IC POC), so the strip opens at the first published IC safety readout; model_first_use_year left null rather than guessed.

safety.model: Rat, mouse and cynomolgus toxicology with joint histology
safety.note: Three-species joint histology found nothing, yet osteonecrosis/RPOA in OA patients triggered the 2010 hold that FDA extended to the IC trials in July 2010.
safety.short: Joint harm missed; IC trials put on hold
safety.quote: The non-clinical investigations we have conducted found no evidence of an effect on the vasculature, bone, or joint in animals treated with large multiples of the clinical dose of tanezumab.
safety.reason: Joint harm not seen in 3-species tox
safety.judgement: Source is Pfizer's briefing document for the 2012 FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee (hosted on fda.gov, archived), not an FDA review or peer-reviewed paper; it states on the same pages: 'On July 16, 2010 FDA informed Pfizer that studies in chronic low back pain, diabetic peripheral neuropathy and interstitial cystitis were also being placed on clinical hold.' The patient-side events were in OA trials; the IC trials logged no adjudicated joint event (NCT00999518: one osteoarthritis SAE, tanezumab 2.5 mg arm) and NCT00999518's registry text says it was terminated 2010-11-16 after the partial hold announced 2010-07-19 'for potential safety issues'. Called contra because the same tox package covered IC patients and FDA applied the hold to them; a retrospective rat medial-meniscal-tear model dosed with tanezumab (LaBranche 2017, doi:10.1136/annrheumdis-2015-208913) reproduced analgesia-driven cartilage damage but 'failed to replicate the hypotrophic bone response observed in tanezumab-treated patients with RPOA'. model_filed left null because the naming document is a sponsor submission, not an FDA review. The OA/NTRK1 draft scores the same signal in its own population.
